newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian 97 customs payments to state to rise 50pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian 97 customs payments to state to rise 50pct.

text.p: Russia's State Customs Committee plans to pay around 70 trillion roubles into federal coffers in 1996, up more than 50 percent on 1996 levels, committee chairman Anatoly Kruglov said on Tuesday.
In 1996 the customs service contributed 46 trillion roubles to the federal budget, slightly more than the planned 43 trillion, he told a news conference.
"For the year as a whole we fulfilled our planned objectives," Kruglov said.
In 1997 customs contributions would total 70 trillion roubles or so, he said.
This represents 16 percent of the total revenues of 434.40 trillion roubles planned in Russia's 1997 budget, which also envisages expenditures of 529.80 trillion.

Of the total 1996 customs contribution of 45.97 trillion roubles, 8.01 trillion roubles came from export taxes, 14.84 trillion from import taxes, 18.39 trillion in value added tax and 4.72 trillion in excise duties, customs figures showed.
Kruglov said that 1996 was a difficult year for the customs service, which had to deal with rising criminal activity in the economic sphere.
The number of customs offences in 1996 nearly doubled from year-ago levels, he said.
